proposals.before: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui is truly the flower of the clan — upon him alone the altars rest. Left Chancellor Hulü Guang mingled the moon, chief minister through generations, his renown ringing in every neighboring realm — and yet, guiltless, he was suddenly destroyed.
proposals.after: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui is truly the flower of the clan — upon him alone the altars rest. Left Chancellor Hulü Mingyue, chief minister through generations, his renown ringing in every neighboring realm — and yet, guiltless, he was suddenly destroyed.
proposals.reason: 斛律明月 (Hulü Mingyue) is Hulü Guang’s courtesy name; 明月 ("bright moon") was mistranslated as the verb phrase "mingled the moon" instead of being rendered as his name.

proposals.before: The emperor was still on the march when Chinu Shi'an set out from Jinyang bearing the victory bulletin toward Pingdu — and met Husixiao Xiaoqing on the way.
proposals.after: The emperor was still on the march when Chinu Shi'an set out from Jinyang bearing the victory bulletin toward Pingdu — and met Husi Xiaoqing on the way.
proposals.reason: 斛斯孝卿’s surname is 斛斯 (Husi); "Husixiao" erroneously merges the surname with the first syllable of the given name 孝卿 (Xiaoqing).

proposals.before: The emperor was on the road; Chinu Shi'an carried the victory bulletin from Jinyang toward Pingdu and encountered Husixiao Xiaoqing.
proposals.after: The emperor was on the road; Chinu Shi'an carried the victory bulletin from Jinyang toward Pingdu and encountered Husi Xiaoqing.
proposals.reason: 斛斯孝卿’s surname is 斛斯 (Husi); "Husixiao" erroneously merges the surname with the first syllable of the given name 孝卿 (Xiaoqing).

proposals.before: Lingshan, Governor of Changle, styled Jingsong, was a clansman younger brother of the Grand Ancestor.
proposals.after: Lingshan, Governor of Changle, styled Jingsong, was a clansman younger brother of Shenwu (Gao Huan).
proposals.reason: 神武 is Gao Huan's temple/epithet Shenwu, not 'Grand Ancestor' (太祖).

proposals.before: He followed the Grand Ancestor in raising troops at Xindu, and ended as Governor of Changle.
proposals.after: He followed Shenwu (Gao Huan) in raising troops at Xindu, and ended as Governor of Changle.
proposals.reason: 神武 should be rendered Shenwu/Gao Huan, not 'Grand Ancestor'.

proposals.before: His son Yi died as commander of the Wuping garrison without heirs; Emperor Wenxuan appointed Fuhu — son of Jianguo, Governor of Qi Province and Lingshan's father's elder brother — to carry on Lingshan's line.
proposals.after: His son Yi died as commander of the Wuping garrison without heirs; Emperor Wenxuan appointed Fuhu — son of Jianguo, Governor of Qi Province and Lingshan's elder paternal cousin — to carry on Lingshan's line.
proposals.reason: 從父兄 means elder paternal cousin (father's brother's son), not father's elder brother.

proposals.after: His son Yi died as commander of the Wuping garrison without heirs; Emperor Wenxuan made Fuhu, son of Jianguo, Governor of Qi Province and Lingshan's elder paternal cousin, successor to Lingshan's line.

decisions.reason: s0117 names 左丞相斛律明月 as a single person; 明月 is Hulü Guang’s courtesy name, not a verb phrase. The before text’s “Hulü Guang mingled the moon” invents an action absent from the Chinese; the proposed “Hulü Mingyue” restores the correct naming.
The literal field has the same error: 斛律明月 is a courtesy-name designation, not “Hulü Guang mingled the moon.” Replacing with “Hulü Mingyue” matches the Chinese.
s0127 has 斛斯孝卿: surname 斛斯 (Husi) and given name 孝卿 (Xiaoqing). “Husixiao Xiaoqing” wrongly fuses the surname with the first syllable of the given name; “Husi Xiaoqing” is correct.
The literal likewise mis-segments 斛斯孝卿 as “Husixiao Xiaoqing.” The proposed “Husi Xiaoqing” correctly separates the two-character surname from the given name.
s0220’s 神武 is Gao Huan’s epithet Shenwu, not 太祖 “Grand Ancestor.” The proposed “Shenwu (Gao Huan)” correctly identifies the referent and aligns with the idiomatic field’s Gao Huan.
s0221’s 從神武 likewise refers to Shenwu/Gao Huan, not a “Grand Ancestor.” The proposed replacement restores the correct designation.
In 靈山從父兄……建國, 從父兄 means Jianguo is Lingshan’s elder paternal cousin (father’s brother’s son), not Lingshan’s father’s elder brother. The proposed kinship term corrects that error.
